newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Supply ship passes tests before Mir docking.
newsitem.headline: Supply ship passes tests before Mir docking.

text.p: A supply ship due to dock with Russia's damaged Mir space station has passed all pre-docking tests, ground control officials said on Monday.

"Progress M-35 (cargo ship) has been tested again during the night and all tests showed it is working," a duty flight operator told Reuters by telephone from Korolyov mission control centre outside Moscow.
He also said the two Russians and American aboard Mir spent a quiet night after preparing for the docking on Sunday. The docking is scheduled for 0559 GMT on Monday.
A previous unmanned Progress craft launched crashed into the station during a manual docking test on June 25 in the worst accident in Mir's 11-year history.
Mir lost up to half its electric power in the collision and experts say this could hamper Monday's docking, which is due to be carried out automatically.

Progress is carrying oxygen, food and water as well as the tools needed to repair the station. There are also parcels from the families of the crew, who have had a nerve-wracking and uncomfortable time since the accident.
